hero.heading: Evidence in practice
hero.subheading: We study the people your AI was not designed for -- and use them to show exactly where your system breaks.
cases.heading: Case studies
cases.card1.title: Adults over 60
cases.card1.desc: The largest demographic gap between AI training data and real-world users. If your system fails here, the problem is bias -- not the user.
cases.card2.title: Children in education
cases.card2.desc: The clearest test of whether explainability is real or performative. If a 12-year-old cannot understand why AI made a decision about them, your transparency is theatre.
cases.card3.title: Patients in clinical AI
cases.card3.desc: The highest-stakes test of fairness. Unexplainable AI recommendations in health settings are an EU AI Act Article 22 issue.
reframe.quote: Older adults are not bad at technology. They are the most accurate test of whether your AI was designed for real people.
reframe.body: If your system fails a 68-year-old retired teacher, it is not her problem to fix.
method.heading: Our method
method.body: We don't study edge cases. We study the populations that reveal systemic failures in AI design: the groups your training data underrepresents, the users your interface wasn't optimised for, the people whose needs expose assumptions you didn't know you'd made.
cta.heading: Want to see the evidence for your system?
cta.body: A bias audit takes days, not months. The findings are always actionable.
